note: Realistic filled-in states in the scoring engine's shape. `expected` is computed by `bin/test-personas --update` and verified by `bin/test-personas`. `hasCriticalFinding` covers only sudden sensorineural loss and marked asymmetry — an isolated conductive-component finding (e.g. otosclerosis) grades only moderate severity via its own dedicated actionable-finding rule and never escalates past 'recommended' follow-up.

personas.name: normal-pure-tone-audiometry-complete
personas.description: A routine pure-tone audiometry check: normal thresholds bilaterally, type A tympanograms, no hearing loss, every mandatory report section present — expect normal classification + none severity + 100% completeness + routine follow-up + no-action.

state.clinicalHistory: Routine hearing check, no otological symptoms.
state.findingsNarrative: Normal hearing thresholds bilaterally across all frequencies tested. Type A tympanograms bilaterally.
state.recommendedFollowUp: No further audiological follow-up required for this indication.

expected.recommendedAction: No specific audiology follow-up required; manage per usual care.

firedRules.description: Normal hearing on an interpretable test with no abnormal structured findings; classified as normal.
No abnormal finding; abnormality severity graded none.
No escalation rule fired; routine follow-up only.

personas.name: abnormal-bilateral-conductive-otosclerosis-moderate-complete
personas.description: Progressive bilateral mild conductive hearing loss with an air-bone gap and type As tympanograms, consistent with otosclerosis: the conductive component is an actionable finding graded moderate severity via its own dedicated rule (not the PTA-severity ladder, since the worst PTA of 38 dB HL stays under the 41 dB moderate threshold), and is deliberately not in `hasCriticalFinding`, so it never escalates past 'recommended' follow-up; report complete — expect abnormal classification + moderate severity (reportingCategory conductive-component) + 100% completeness + recommended follow-up + specialist-referral.

state.clinicalHistory: Progressive bilateral hearing loss over several years; family history of otosclerosis.
state.findingsNarrative: Bilateral mild conductive hearing loss with an air-bone gap; type As tympanograms bilaterally, in keeping with otosclerosis.
state.impression: Bilateral mild conductive hearing loss consistent with otosclerosis.
state.recommendedFollowUp: Refer to ENT for consideration of hearing-aid fitting or stapedectomy.

expected.recommendedAction: Recommend hearing-aid assessment or specialist referral as clinically indicated.

firedRules.description: One or more abnormal structured findings are present; classified as abnormal.
An actionable abnormal finding (hearing loss present or conductive component) is present; severity graded moderate.

flags.description: Hearing loss is present and may require timely management.
flags.suggestedAction: Ensure the referrer is alerted and a clear management plan is documented.

flags.description: A conductive component is present and may warrant ENT referral.
flags.suggestedAction: Consider referral to ENT for assessment of the conductive component.

personas.name: critical-sudden-sensorineural-loss-uncommunicated-incomplete
personas.description: Sudden-onset right-sided sensorineural hearing loss over 48 hours, a 30 dB or greater drop across three contiguous frequencies versus the unaffected left ear: this critical finding (sudden SNHL, an otological emergency, plus the marked asymmetry it produces) auto-escalates classification to critical and follow-up to critical-alert regardless of the other axes; the result has not yet been recorded as communicated, no originating request is linked, and the clinical history and impression sections are not yet completed while urgent treatment is arranged — expect critical classification + major severity + 60% completeness + critical-alert follow-up + urgent-review.

state.findingsNarrative: Sudden-onset right-sided sensorineural hearing loss over the past 48 hours, with a 30 dB or greater drop across three contiguous frequencies compared to the unaffected left ear.
state.clinicianNotes: Phoned through to the on-call ENT team immediately; urgent oral corticosteroids being arranged.

expected.recommendedAction: Refer urgently to ENT as an otological emergency and communicate the critical result to the referrer now.

firedRules.description: A critical structured finding (sudden sensorineural hearing loss or marked asymmetry) is present; classified as critical.
Critical finding present; abnormality severity graded major.
Mandatory report section missing: clinical history.
Critical finding (sudden sensorineural loss or marked asymmetry) auto-escalates follow-up urgency to critical-alert regardless of the other axes.

flags.description: A critical finding (sudden sensorineural hearing loss or marked asymmetry) is present.
flags.suggestedAction: Communicate the critical result to the referrer immediately and document the communication.

flags.description: Critical finding present but the result has not been recorded as communicated.
flags.suggestedAction: Contact the referrer now and record who was informed, with date and time.

flags.description: Result is consistent with sudden sensorineural hearing loss (otological emergency).
flags.suggestedAction: Refer urgently to ENT; consider high-dose corticosteroids per local guidance.

flags.description: Marked asymmetry between ears (red flag for retrocochlear pathology).
flags.suggestedAction: Refer to ENT for MRI of the internal auditory meatus to exclude vestibular schwannoma.

flags.description: No impression / conclusion has been recorded.
flags.suggestedAction: Add an impression that answers the clinical question.

flags.description: A significant finding is present but no originating request reference is recorded.
flags.suggestedAction: Link the report to the originating request to support discrepancy review.
